title: Exactness of actual scalar localization on module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $s\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$ be a global section. Use the abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $R_s=R[1/s]$, the sheafification of $V\mapsto R(V)[1/s|_V]$, with its canonical ring map $\varphi:R\to R_s$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Let $E:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_s)$ be actual change of rings $E(M)=R_s\otimes_R M$, using sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $E(f)=1\otimes f$ on morphisms. Then $E$ is additive and exact: it preserves finite limits and finite colimits, or equivalently sends every short exact sequence of $R$-module sheaves to a short exact sequence of $R_s$-module sheaves. The same assertion holds for any functor equipped with a natural isomorphism to this actual change-of-rings functor. No point, enough-points, scheme, nonzero, or boundedness hypothesis is imposed.

PresheafOfModules.evaluationJointlyReflectsLimits assembles these sectionwise limit cones into finite-limit preservation of tensorRight P. This also handles empty finite diagrams.

proof.text: Let A be module sheafification over R and I its fully faithful right adjoint. Both preserve finite limits. The monoidal sheafification comparison A followed by tensorRight (A P) is isomorphic to tensorRight P followed by A. Precompose with I and use the invertible counit I A ≅ id to prove that tensorRight (A P) preserves finite limits. This is the private independent-universe proof of the needed special case of 03ET, without the fixed-universe upstream interface. The existing ringedLocalizationRing_moduleComparisonOfUniverses identifies restriction of scalars of the localized ring unit with A P; symmetry gives finite-limit preservation of left tensoring with that restricted unit B.

source.place: Tags 03ES, 03ET and 03DB; Section 03EK; Algebra Tag 00HT for localization flatness.

proof.text: Construct the scalar-extension presheaf functor from changeOfRingsPresheafOfUniverses, mapping arrows by sectionwise ModuleCat.extendScalars, and compose with target module sheafification to obtain E. On underlying abelian presheaves this is naturally isomorphic to left tensoring with B.val: the component is the identity, and compatibility with restriction is the changeOfRingsMap_tmulOfUniverses formula. The monoidal sheafification comparison and invertible counit then give a natural isomorphism E followed by the target forgetful functor ≅ tensorLeft B followed by the source forgetful functor. The object and map formulas in the statement hold definitionally.

source.place: Tags 03ES, 03ET and 03DB; Section 03EK; Algebra Tag 00HT for localization flatness.

proof.text: Left tensoring with B is additive and preserves finite colimits by the existing independent-universe tensor API. Both forgetful functors to abelian sheaves are faithful, additive and preserve finite limits and colimits. They reflect finite limits and colimits. Transfer all three properties along the isomorphism in step 4 and reflect them to E. No assertion that a sheaf epimorphism is surjective on sections is used.

source.place: Tags 03ES, 03ET and 03DB; Section 03EK; Algebra Tag 00HT for localization flatness.

proof.text: For F naturally isomorphic to E, apply Mathlib Functor.additive_of_iso, preservesFiniteLimits_of_natIso and preservesFiniteColimits_of_natIso to the inverse isomorphism. Together with the explicit construction and formulas for E this supplies every conjunct of the unchanged statement.
